newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 3.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
* Alan Levine resigned as president of Sony Pictures Entertainment of Sony Corp amid speculation that he would be replaced by producer and studio executive John Calley.
* Service Corp International has presented shareholders of Loewen Group Inc with a hostile $3.2 billion bid after its previous offer was rejected.
* Toys R Us Inc said it would buy Baby Superstore Inc for about $376 million in stock.
* Household Finance Corp of Household International Inc has launched a lobbying campaign in U.S. Congress to try to avoid having to pay a levy on its operations in the savings and loan sector.
* Morgan Stanley Group Inc reported a 4.8 percent increase in third-quarter earnings, citing healthy revenues from investment banking, securities trading and asset management.

* The U.S. Securities and Exchange Comission appears to have decided not to bring securities fraud charges against the Denver International Airport and its underwriters in a case involving whether bond buyers were intentionally misled about potential problems at the new airport.
* The bull run market on Wall Street is the biggest in history without a decline of at least 10 percent, given the latest rise in the Dow Jones industrial average of 29.07 to 5,933.97.
* Overseas buying and good U.S. economic indicators have helped the price of treasury securities to rise to a six-week high.
